p: your bodies are bodies of clay" (Iyov 13:12).
HaKadosh Baruch Hu said to Yisrael:
'You shall blot out the remembrance of Amalek,'
אִם זְכִיתֶם אַתֶּם בָּנָיו שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם
if you are worthy, you are the children of Avraham,
who likened himself to ashes, etc.;
prepare yourselves for the bondage of Egypt,
as it says (Shemos 1:14), 'And they embittered' etc."
The matter is as we said above,
that the kelipah of Amalek stands opposed
against the holiness of the root,
and this is "if you are worthy,
you are the children of Avraham,"
who attained the aspect of Atika
וְדַיְיקָא עַל יְדֵי שֶׁהִמְשִׁיל עַצְמוֹ כְּאֵפֶר
and specifically through likening himself to ashes,
מָרוֹם וְקָדוֹשׁ אֶשְׁכּוֹן וְאֶת דַּכָּא וְגוֹמֵר
"I dwell on high and in holiness, and with the contrite" etc.;
מָרוֹם וְקָדוֹשׁ מוֹרֶה עַל בְּחִינַת עַתִּיקָא.
"on high and in holiness" denotes the aspect of Atika.
in Torah she'b'al peh as well
as we said (and it was explained there);
and this is what the bondage of Egypt alludes to,
as it says, "And they embittered their lives
וְאִיתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א כז, א וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת)
and it is stated (Zohar I 27a and elsewhere):
'and with all labor in the field'—this is Baraisa;
They further said in the Midrash:
"your bodies are bodies of clay" (Iyov ibid.)—
like the Generation of the Dispersion,
וְהַחֵמָר הָיָה לָהֶם לַחוֹמֶר [בְּרֵאשִׁית יא, ג]
"and the slime served them as mortar" (Bereishis 11:3);
see there, and in Pesikta Rabbasi
And one can also find an allusion
for the matter of the exposition of "your remembrances"
as referring to the remembrances of Amalek,
וְעַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה כו, א)
based on what they said (Shemos Rabbah 26:1):
"I was not at ease from the first decree
וְהֶעֱמִיד לִי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא גּוֹאֵל
and HaKadosh Baruch Hu set up for me a redeemer—
this is Miriam, named for the bitterness;
and I had no quiet from the second decree,
'If it is a son, you shall kill him,'
וְהֶעֱמִיד לִי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא גּוֹאֵל
and HaKadosh Baruch Hu set up for me a redeemer—
this is Aharon, named for the pregnancy;
and I had no rest from the third decree,
שֶׁגָּזַר כָּל הַבֵּן הַיִּלּוֹד הַיְאוֹרָה וְגוֹמֵר
which he decreed: 'Every son that is born, into the river' etc.,
and HaKadosh Baruch Hu set up a redeemer
עַל שֵׁם הַמַּיִם זֶה מֹשֶׁה כּוּלֵּי
named for the water—this is Moshe," etc.;
And it can be said that these three decrees
were in order to refine in Egypt
the crown of Torah through Moshe,
the crown of priesthood through Aharon,
and the crown of kingship through Miriam;
בָּתֵּי מַלְכוּת דָּוִד נַמֵּי מִמִּרְיָם קָאָתֵי.
we call it Torah she'b'al peh
and it is the aspect of Miriam's well,
which alludes to Torah she'b'al peh,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (יַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי חֻקַּת רֶמֶז תשסד)
as they said (Yalkut Shimoni, Chukas, remez 764)
עַל פָּסוּק וְדִבַּרְתֶּם אֶל הַסֶּלַע [בַּמִּדְבָּר כ, ח]
on the verse "And you shall speak to the rock" (Bamidbar 20:8):
and it will bring forth water from the rock"
(and it was explained in Terumah, maamar 11,
in the passage beginning "And in the Gemara"; see there).
And it is stated in the writings of the Arizal
that the bondage of Egypt was
to refine the souls of the Generation of the Flood,
the Generation of the Dispersion, and the people of Sodom;
וְיֵשׁ לוֹמַר שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן נֶגֶד
and it can be said that these too correspond to
שְׁלֹשָׁה בֵּירוּרִים שֶׁל הַשְּׁלֹשָׁה גּוֹאֲלִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל.
the three refinements of the three aforementioned redeemers.
The decree "Into the river you shall cast him,"
the refinement of the Generation of the Flood,
is the refinement of the Written Torah
שֶׁהָיָה רָאוּי מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
since Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom, was fit
to give them the Torah in the Generation of the Flood,
as they said in the Raaya Mehemna
וְכֵן אִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה ל, יג)
and so it is stated in the Midrash (Shemos Rabbah 30:13)
that they said, "And knowledge of Your ways
לֹא חָפָצְנוּ [אִיּוֹב כא, יד] זֶה תּוֹרָה.
we do not desire" (Iyov 21:14)—this is Torah.
שֶׁהִיא דְּרָכָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
which is the ways of HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
Who decrees a decree and fulfills it first,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה שָׁם, ט וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת)
as they said (Shemos Rabbah ibid. 9, and elsewhere),
He tells Yisrael to do, etc.
And this is what it says (Bereishis 6:3),
as they said in the holy Zohar (there)
to allude that he is destined to refine them.
And the decree "And they embittered" etc., "with clay and with bricks,"
which came for the sin of the Generation of the Dispersion,
הוּא נֶגֶד בֵּירוּר בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
corresponds to the refinement of the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh
עַל יְדֵי מִרְיָם שֶׁנִּקְרֵאת עַל שֵׁם הַמָּרוֹר
through Miriam, who is named for the bitterness;
And the main founding of Torah she'b'al peh
as has been explained many times from the Gemara
וְשָׁם מָצְאוּ הַבִּקְעָה בְּאֶרֶץ שִׁנְעָר [בְּרֵאשִׁית יא, ב]
and there they found the valley in the land of Shinar (Bereishis 11:2),
and by means of this wisdom
they wanted to make a name for themselves,
and they succeeded in this with the opposing power,
"And now nothing will be withheld from them" etc.
וּגְזֵירַת אִם בֵּן הוּא וַהֲמִיתֶן אוֹתוֹ
And the decree "If it is a son, you shall kill him"
is to refine the blemish of the people of Sodom,
שֶׁהָיָה בָּהֶן צָרוּת עַיִן עַל הָעֲנִיִּים
who were stingy toward the poor
וְלֹא גָּמְלוּ חֶסֶד כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר [יְחֶזְקֵאל טז, מט]
and did not do kindness, as it says (Yechezkel 16:49),
"And the hand of the poor and needy she did not strengthen."
וּבָזֶה הָיָה הַבֵּירוּר עַל יְדֵי אַהֲרֹן
And here the refinement was through Aharon,
for he loved peace and pursued peace,
אוֹהֵב אֶת הַבְּרִיּוֹת כּוּלֵּי [אָבוֹת פֶּרֶק א מִשְׁנָה יב].
of the Generation of the Flood and the Generation of the Dispersion
לָכֵן נִצְרָךְ לִסְבּוֹל קוֹשִׁי הַגְּזֵירָה זְמַן רַב
therefore it was necessary to bear the hardship of the decree for a long time,
in order to refine and purify the souls
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן פְּגַם דְּאַנְשֵׁי סְדוֹם
whereas the blemish of the people of Sodom,
therefore there also did not persist
the decree "If it is a son" etc.;
רַק הָיָה דַּי לָהֶם בְּצַעַר לְפִי שָׁעָה
rather, a passing distress sufficed for them,
when Pharaoh decreed to the midwives,
and his decree was not carried out,

paragraphs.text: Zohar I 27a, Bereshit 24:3 — “With regard to the holy limbs of the body, which are from the side of good, it is said, ‘They came to Marah and could not drink water from Marah.’ In this manner the masters of the Mishnah said: ‘They embittered their lives with hard labor’—with a difficulty; ‘with mortar’—with an a-fortiori inference; ‘with bricks’—with clarification of the law; ‘with every labor in the field’—this is baraita; ‘all their labor’—this is Mishnah.” The terms of Egyptian labor are read as forms of effort in Oral Torah. Rav Tzadok uses this original wordplay to explain another mode of overcoming Amalek.

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 26:1 — “‘I was not at ease’—from the first decree Pharaoh decreed against me: ‘They embittered their lives’; the Holy One raised up a redeemer—Miriam, named for the bitterness. ‘I was not quiet’—from the second decree, ‘If it is a son, kill him’; the Holy One raised up a redeemer—Aaron, named for pregnancy. ‘I did not rest’—from the third decree, ‘Every son who is born, cast into the river’; the Holy One raised up a redeemer named for the water—Moses, as it is said, ‘For from the water I drew him.’ ‘And agitation came’—this is Amalek.” The three decrees and three redeemers are explicitly paired in the Midrash; their correspondence to three crowns is Rav Tzadok’s next interpretive step.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Likkutei Maamarim, Inyan Shimshon 4 — “The clouds of glory were for them a surrounding light, and the well and the manna an inner light, which are the three crowns of Torah, kehunah and malchus that Moshe, Aharon and Miriam merited.” Rav Tzadok there maps the three redeemers onto the levels of light. Malchus, Miriam’s crown, is the last level, the nefesh, and as the final level it is the head of what follows. This fits Miriam’s link to Torah she’b’al peh here.

paragraphs.text: Sotah 11b:22 — “‘Because the midwives feared God, He made houses for them.’ Rav and Samuel: one said, houses of priesthood and Levite service; the other said, royal houses. According to the one who says houses of priesthood and Levite service: Aaron and Moses. According to the one who says royal houses: David too descended from Miriam, as it is written, ‘Azubah died, and Caleb took Ephrath, and she bore him Hur’; and it is written, ‘David was the son of that Ephrathite man.’” The teaching establishes Miriam’s place in the ancestry of kingship, supporting the third crown in Rav Tzadok’s sequence.

paragraphs.text: Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 763:18 — “When this rock was small, you struck it, as it is said, ‘Strike the rock.’ But now, ‘Speak to the rock’: recite one chapter over it, and it will bring out water from the rock.” The parable compares the change from striking to speaking with the education of a child as he grows. paragraphs.text: Shaar HaPesukim, Shemot, opening exposition and paragraph 47 — “All those spirits ... were lofty, holy souls from the aspect of knowledge, which became mixed among the husks and required many reincarnations to refine and whiten them until their contamination was ended. ... The beginning of their reincarnation was in the generation of the Flood. ... Afterward they reincarnated a second time in the generation of the dispersion. ... Afterward they reincarnated a third time among the people of Sodom. ... Although the wilderness generation had been repaired and the good separated from the evil, their original contamination had not wholly ceased until they stood at Mount Sinai. ... Even though they had received their punishment in the exile of Egypt, they needed actively to return and fulfill those commandments they had transgressed.” This verifies the three generations and their Egyptian purification. The same work separately marks a speculative reconstruction with “I am uncertain”; that qualification is retained in the full provenance rather than being turned into an unqualified statement by the Ari.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III 216b, Pinchas 10:16 — “Furthermore, the rabbis established another mystery: the generation that goes is the generation that comes. If one departed lame, one came lame; if one departed blind, one came blind. The rabbis further established that Moses was destined to receive the Torah in the generation of the Flood, but because they were wicked, this is what is written: ‘For he too is flesh’—be-shagam is Moses. Why is he called be-shagam? ... Kohelet removed the bet from be-shagam to conceal the matter: ‘I said that this too is vanity.’” The equivalence of be-shagam and Moshe is numerical. Chullin 139b likewise asks “Where is Moses in the Torah?” and answers with this verse.

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 30:13 — “Rabbi Aha said: The Holy One, blessed be He, wished to give them four things—Torah, afflictions, sacrificial service, and prayer—and they did not wish for them. ‘They said to God: Depart from us’—these are afflictions. ‘We do not desire knowledge of Your ways’—this is Torah. ‘What is the Almighty that we should serve Him?’—these are sacrifices. ‘What benefit will we have if we entreat Him?’—this is prayer. The Holy One said to them: What caused you to be lost from the evening of this world and the morning of the world to come? Because you did not accept the Torah, which contains justice.” The passage specifically discusses the generation of the Flood and its rejection of divine instruction.

paragraphs.text: Shemot Rabbah 30:9 — “The measure of the Holy One, blessed be He, is unlike that of flesh and blood. Flesh and blood instructs others to act while doing nothing himself; the Holy One is not so. Rather, what He does, He tells Israel to do and to observe.” Rav Tzadok therefore understands Torah as God’s own ways, not merely as instructions detached from the divine conduct.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Menachem Nachum of Chernobyl, Meor Einayim, Miketz, s.v. Kidivreichem ken hu — “The generations of Enosh, the Flood, and the Dispersion acted wickedly in a way that reached the highest levels: they separated the world and the Torah from Hashem, so to speak, and the Torah fell into Egypt’s forces of impurity. This was heard from the holy teacher R. Dov Ber and is also explained in the Ari’s writings. Thus their labor was ‘with mortar and bricks’: as explained in the Zohar, ‘mortar’ signifies inference from minor to major and ‘bricks’ the clarification of halachah. Through their labor in treading mortar they extracted from Egypt’s forces of impurity the kal vachomer, one of the thirteen methods by which Torah is expounded; similarly with the bricks.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Meor Einayim explains the repair enacted by the Zohar’s wordplay: the bodily labor releases powers of Torah reasoning held in exile after the earlier generations’ damage. This develops Rav Tzadok’s association of the Dispersion, Egyptian mortar and bricks, and the clarification of Oral Torah. Meor Einayim’s list includes Enosh; Rav Tzadok’s threefold arrangement here includes Sodom.

paragraphs.text: Sukkah 20a:11 — “When Torah was first forgotten from Israel, Ezra came up from Babylonia and established it. It was forgotten again; Hillel the Babylonian came up and established it. It was forgotten again; Rabbi Hiyya and his sons came up and established it.” The recurring Babylonian restoration of Torah supplies Rav Tzadok’s historical basis for linking Oral Torah with the place of the dispersion.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Sukkos 23 — “The souls of the generation of the Dispersion were from the root of Torah she’b’al peh — ‘it is not in Heaven’… From this came their kelipah, to wage war against Hashem.” Rav Tzadok there explains the “opposing power”: the authority of Torah she’b’al peh, which can “defeat” Heaven, turned in them into a rebellious ascent to the heavens. Their mutual love is why a remnant survived.
